stories.title: Beyond Borders: Reassessing the Recognition and Protection of 'Climate Refugees' in International Law.
stories.description: This article examines the complex issue of "climate refugees," referring to people forced to migrate across borders due to the impacts of climate change, and the challenges surrounding their legal recognition and protection under international refugee and environmental law. It highlights that existing international instruments, such as the 1951 Refugee Convention and its 1967 Protocol, do not recognize climate change or environmental factors as grounds for refugee status, creating a "recognitional void" that leaves climate-induced migrants without clear legal protection. The article discusses the multifaceted causes of climate-induced migration, including sudden environmental disasters and slower-onset changes like sea-level rise, and the difficulties in identifying agents of persecution and applying traditional refugee definitions. It also reviews regional initiatives and non-binding frameworks, such as the Bangkok Principles and the Nansen Initiative, which attempt to address these gaps, while emphasizing the need for coordinated international and regional cooperation to develop effective legal and policy responses to this growing humanitarian challenge.

stories.title: Reconciling strong coordination and anion-reinforced solvation structure enables nonflammable electrolytes for potassium-ion batteries
stories.description: Nonflammable electrolytes are pivotal for improving the safety of potassium-ion batteries. However, their broad adoption has been hindered by the inadequate electrode compatibility of conventional nonflammable electrolytes, which typically result from strong solvation and excessive free solvent molecules. Here, we employ a molecular design strategy that integrates strong coordination capability with anion-reinforced solvation structure, thereby enabling the effective deployment of nonflammable phosphate solvents. By incorporating lengthened functionalized side-chains into the phosphate backbone, the tailored molecule tri(2-butoxyethyl) phosphate achieves robust multi-site chelation via synergistic interactions between the ether oxygen (C-O-C) and the phosphoryl (P=O) groups. Concurrently, its large molecular structure effectively increases the anion-to-solvent ratio in the electrolyte, promoting the formation of stable electrode-electrolyte interphases, and resulting in high compatibility with both the negative and positive electrodes. Consequently, the optimized tri(2-butoxyethyl) phosphate-based electrolyte enables stable cycling of graphite negative electrode (92.7% capacity retention after 800 cycles at 100 mA g−1) and Prussian blue positive electrode (4.2 V, 88.6% capacity retention after 3200 cycles at 100 mA g−1). Furthermore, the assembled graphite||Prussian blue full cell also maintains 80.3% capacity retention after 1500 cycles at 500 mA g−1. This work provides a strategy for electrolyte design in potassium-ion batteries. Nonflammable electrolytes are key to safe potassium-ion batteries but suffer from poor electrode compatibility. Here, authors design a phosphate molecule with long side-chains enabling strong chelation and anion-reinforced solvation, leading to high electrode compatibility.

stories.title: From sucking worms to Windkessel: The physics of an early eighteenth century firefighting device.
stories.description: This article focuses on the physics and modeling of the "Windkessel effect," originally an airtight chamber used in piston-driven water pumps to smooth the pulsatile output flow, with a detailed case study of Richard Newsham's 1725 fire engine. The authors develop a simple analytical model describing how the Windkessel compresses and expands trapped air to regulate water flow, reducing output variation from about 80% without the device to approximately 16% with it. Using historical data and physical parameters from surviving Newsham fire engines, the study quantifies the Windkessel's effectiveness and discusses assumptions such as isothermal air compression and negligible pipe resistance. The paper highlights the Windkessel's longstanding practical utility in fire engines and modern well systems, noting that despite its significance, it has been largely overlooked in physics education literature.

stories.title: Series Model That Scores Full 42 Points in IMO
stories.description: While advanced AI systems have demonstrated exceptional proficiency in solving complex Mathematical Olympiad problems, showcasing remarkable logical reasoning and computational capabilities, these intelligent algorithms still face critical gaps in mastering the nuanced, unstructured scenarios of real daily life. Unlike the rule-bound, clearly defined constraints of competitive math challenges, everyday human interactions, context-dependent decision-making, ambiguous social cues, and adaptive problem-solving for unforeseen real-world situations require AI to develop embodied common sense, contextual awareness, and flexible reasoning frameworks that go beyond specialized domain expertise. This gap highlights a key frontier in modern artificial intelligence development: bridging the divide between superhuman performance in narrow, high-stakes academic competitions and the robust, intuitive "getting by" skills that humans navigate seamlessly in routine daily living.
